correctness.rationale: The proof reduces a rightmost failure of the interval-completeness inequalities to a reverse-tree set with at least five positive distances. A zero-suffix lemma rules out the only smaller tail, and earlier reverse folds cannot reduce cardinality. This gives the sharp defective-width lower bound 10, from which the near-minimum equivalence and anti-diagonal classification follow. Exact integer enumeration through length 10 agrees with the published total counts and checks every stated low-width form.

originality.rationale: Muney's 2026 paper explicitly leaves the classification of sequences with extension width at most 9 as an open question. Searches across valid-extension, extension-width, anti-diagonal, near-minimum, Gilbreath, and synonymous formulations found no matching theorem or later solution. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from very recent or incompletely indexed follow-up work.

value.rationale: The result resolves an explicit open question, proves a sharp gap between interval-complete and defective near-minimum extension sets, and gives a complete structural classification of widths 5, 7, and 9 by the right anti-diagonal.
